transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what finally made me come in is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months now. There are these stretches where I'll just skip dinner entirely, and I've actually lost some weight without even trying to. And then on other nights, I just... I end up picking at crackers or having a bowl of cereal, mostly because the thought of actually cooking a meal for myself just feels completely pointless lately.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends or family?

Yes, I have. I mean, I still try to go through the motions of things I used to really love doing... like watering the garden or showing up to my book club. But lately, most of the time it just feels completely flat. I'm there, but I'm not really enjoying it, and I usually end up leaving early. Or, with some things, I just... I end up not even starting them at all.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have these feelings been present most days, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

It's been going on for a while now. I'd say... well, it really started since the divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago. And yes, to answer your question, it's definitely present most days. Pretty much every day since then, really.
Can you describe a time when you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Well, I think I just answered that, but... yes. It's been pretty much every day since my divorce was finalized, which was a year and seven months ago. It's not just a two-week thing for me, it's been a constant feeling for a long time now. Most of the day, nearly every day.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two years now?
Well, no, not quite two years. Like I said, it's been about a year and seven months since the divorce was finalized. But since then, yes, it's been most of the day, nearly every day.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two years now?
No, not two years. Like I mentioned, it's been about a year and seven months. That's when the divorce was finalized, and it's been pretty constant since then.
Have you had days when you felt down or depressed that lasted for two years or more, even if they weren't every day?

No, it hasn't been two years at all. I know we keep coming back to that timeframe, but... this has really only been going on since the divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago. Before that, I wasn't feeling this way, even just on and off.
Have you had any periods of time, even before the divorce, when you felt down or depressed most days for two years or more?

No, I really haven't. Before the divorce, I was actually doing fine. I mean, I had bad days like anyone else, but never anything that lasted for years or even months at a time. It's just been this past year and a half or so.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely optimistic, even if others thought you were not acting like yourself?
No, I've never felt like that. I've never had a time where I felt unusually high or overly energetic. Just... just the opposite lately.
Since the divorce, have you had trouble sleeping or sleeping too much nearly every day?

Yeah, I definitely have trouble staying asleep. I can usually get into bed at a reasonable hour just fine, but... I end up waking up around four in the morning. My mind just starts going, thinking about bills, my work notes, or the divorce. And then I just lie there, feeling completely exhausted, until the alarm finally goes off.
Since the divorce, have you felt feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt nearly every day?

Yes, I do. I just keep replaying the marriage in my head, and... I tell myself I must have failed at something really basic. I mean, part of me knows that relationships are much more complicated than that, but it's hard not to feel guilty about it every day.
Since the divorce, have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, nearly every day?

Yes, I have. I mean, I still try to go through the motions of things I used to love doing. Like... I'll go out to water the garden, or I'll show up to my book club. But most of the time, it just feels really flat. I don't get any joy out of it anymore, and I usually end up leaving early, or sometimes I just... can't bring myself to start at all.
Since the divorce, have you felt fatigued or had a loss of energy nearly every day?

Yes, almost every day. It's... I just don't have the energy I used to. Even on days when my caseload at the hospital isn't unusually heavy, I feel like I'm just dragging my body through the halls. And then when I finally get home, I'm just too tired to do anything. I can't bring myself to cook, or do my normal stretches, or even answer personal messages from friends. I just feel completely drained by the time I walk through the door.
Since the divorce, have you experienced a change in your appetite or weight nearly every day?

Yes, actually... that's what finally made me make this appointment. My appetite has been all over the place for months now. There are stretches where I just skip dinner entirely, and I've lost weight without even trying to. And then other nights, I just pick at some crackers or a bowl of cereal... mostly because the idea of cooking a meal just for myself feels completely pointless.

inference_history.note: The patient reported symptoms lasting more than a year and seven months, which supports the possibility of persistent depressive disorder (F33.9) rather than just major depressive disorder (F32.9). However, the duration and chronic nature of symptoms have narrowed the candidates by ruling out F50.0 (Anorexia Nervosa), as the eating disturbances described are better explained by mood disorder.

The patient has experienced a persistently depressed mood for about a year and seven months following a divorce, with loss of interest and appetite changes. This rules out F32.9 (major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified) as the duration exceeds typical acute episodes and suggests a recurrent or persistent pattern. However, F33.1 (recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms) becomes a more likely candidate given the chronic nature and severity of symptoms. F33.9 (depressive disorder, unspecified) remains as a differential due to insufficient clarity on episode severity and functional impairment.

The patient continues to report a persistent depressed mood since the divorce (about 1 year and 7 months ago), without any history of manic or hypomanic episodes. The duration of symptoms supports the diagnosis of recurrent depressive disorder, current episode prolonged, but there is not yet enough information to distinguish between mild, moderate, or severe without psychotic features. Further questioning is needed to determine the severity and to rule out other conditions.
